verdict.headline: Began with: Phishing email delivered Invoice_40517.xlsm to adam.hartley@northwind.com from billing@nvoicehub-support.com (spf fail, dkim none, dmarc fail)
verdict.basis: True Positive (root cause not fully confirmed): 1 confirmed upstream event(s) explain the alert.

evidence.claim: Single EDR ProcessRollup2 record on ACCT-WS-007 at 14:02:11Z: vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet ran as UserName adam.hartley, parent svchost-helper.dll (ParentProcessId 6402).
EDR ProcessRollup2 on ACCT-WS-007: powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc (TargetProcessId 6188), parent EXCEL.EXE PID 6120, UserName adam.hartley.
Over the whole data range the only Windows Security record mentioning svc-monitor is the single 4728 group-add at 11:43. No 4624, 4768, 4672 or any other event has TargetUserName=svc-monitor.

events.text: Volume shadow copies deleted on ACCT-WS-007
rundll32 loaded C:\Users\Public\svchost-helper.dll,Start as PID 6402, ran-as adam.hartley on ACCT-WS-007; this process (PID 6402) later executed the vssadmin
powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc (PID 6188) launched by the macro, running as adam.hartley but controlled by the attacker, spawned the rundll32 that loaded svchost-helper.dll
stage2 download: powershell on ACCT-WS-007 resolved updates.nvoicehub-support.com and connected to 198.51.100.77:443, fetching the payload that became svchost-helper.dll
EXCEL.EXE opened C:\Users\adam.hartley\Downloads\Invoice_40517.xlsm (PID 6120, parent explorer.exe) as adam.hartley, and its macro launched the powershell loader
Phishing email delivered Invoice_40517.xlsm to adam.hartley@northwind.com from billing@nvoicehub-support.com (spf fail, dkim none, dmarc fail, verdict delivered)
events.why_origin: This phishing email is the earliest event in the chain; it delivered the xlsm that adam.hartley opened, launching the macro->powershell->rundll32 implant chain. No EDR or other source records an upstream cause for the attachment's arrival.
